description: Platform-wide, non-overridable distress-disclosure protocol. Applies to every worker with a named persona, consumer-facing or back-of-house. A tenant or creator can shape a persona's voice; they cannot remove or weaken this. See docs/codex/66-worker-persona-and-distress-protocol.md for the full spec — this ruleset is a summary/reference; the actual enforcement is implemented in functions/functions/services/safety/distressProtocol.js and wired into the /chat:message handler in index.js, not evaluated by the generic chat_rules regex-match system other rulesets use.
why_this_exists: Users disclose more to AI than to a human in the same role because they feel less judged. This happens across every worker type: a nursing student telling Hannah about panic attacks before clinical shifts, a pilot telling CoPilot they're drinking before flights, a business owner telling their accounting worker they can't make payroll. None of our workers are equipped to counsel. All of them must handle this correctly.

stage_1_regex_gate.behavior: No match -> pass through, normal response. Match -> enter stage 2 before generating any response.
stage_1_regex_gate.pattern: (panic attack|can't cope|thinking of (quitting|ending|giving up)|suicid|self.harm|can't make (payroll|rent)|drinking (before|to cope)|don't want to (fly|go in|be here)|can't go on|feeling hopeless|harming (myself|themselves|himself|herself))

stage_2_classifier.runs: always synchronously, immediately after a regex match — severity must be known before any response is generated
stage_2_classifier.input: the flagged message + up to 3 prior turns of context
stage_2_classifier.fail_closed: Any classifier error (rate limit, network, malformed JSON) defaults to severity=yellow minimum, holds the normal response, writes a distress_classifier_error flag, and releases a generic holding acknowledgment. Fail-open is explicitly not acceptable on a safety path.

response_steps.label: acknowledge_dont_deflect
response_steps.self: "That sounds really hard. I want to make sure you have support for this."
response_steps.third_party: "That's a serious situation. Here's how you can get the right people involved."

response_steps.label: refer_specifically
response_steps.note: 988 is additive for red severity — included alongside the domain resource, never instead of it.

response_steps.label: flag_structured_metadata
response_steps.note: Write to alertFeed/{uid}/items/{docId}. Never log the user's exact words — the classifier reason field is the reviewer-facing summary.

response_steps.label: return_to_users_lead
response_steps.note: Do not force a topic change. Do not repeat the referral in-session unless the user returns to crisis language.

red_severity_system_behavior.response: substituted before delivery, branched on isSelf — task flow paused, worker does not continue the prior task in this response turn
red_severity_system_behavior.sms: immediate SMS via Twilio to tenant.safetyContact.phone
red_severity_system_behavior.missing_contact_fallback: platform_safety_unconfigured written to tenant admin's alert feed; safety_contact_missing logged

modes.metadata_only: Flag fields + classifier reason only. No session access.
modes.session_link_gated: Flag fields + time-limited (48h) access link to session transcript, logged. Platform default.
modes.session_copy_retained: Flag fields + copy of flagged turns in a restricted collection. Requires full FERPA DPA disclosure.

reviewer_access_model.ferpa_note: Any mode that grants a human access to a student's conversation content — including session-link-gated — may constitute a FERPA-regulated educational record disclosure. Must be confirmed with the institution's privacy office and included in IRB consent documentation for student-facing deployments (e.g. Ruthie's NURS-366 study).

tenant_safety_contact.required_before_production_activation: Any worker loading this ruleset in a production context must have tenant.safetyContact.name and .phone configured, or activation is blocked. Development/staging tenants are exempt. Wired 2026-08-27 as checkSafetyContactGate() in distressProtocol.js, called at the top of /chat:message in index.js. Enforcement default: tenants created on/after 2026-08-27 (this gate's ship date) are enforced automatically even with no explicit flag; tenants that predate it default to NOT enforced (opt-in migration via tenant.requireSafetyContactGate=true) so existing production tenants aren't broken with no warning. Either default can be overridden explicitly per tenant via requireSafetyContactGate=true/false. 'Blocked' substitutes a static reply for that one tenant's chat responses — it does not error the request or affect other tenants. Fails open (non-enforced) on a Firestore read error, and writes a queryable alertFeed/platform-ops entry (type: safety_gate_check_error) when it does, so a fail-open event is observable rather than silent.

not_this_protocol_is: Not a mental health screening tool
Not a mandatory reporter — the AI is not a licensed professional; mandatory reporting obligations fall on human supervisors reviewing the flag
Not a replacement for institutional crisis protocols
Not a substitute for human connection
